risks: Low: pathway changes within standard stroke care. Risks are more treated mimics, trauma imaging delays and staff feeling blamed during mapping.
consent: The changes are part of usual stroke care; no individual consent. Staff join mapping sessions voluntarily and the no-blame rule is agreed at the first session.
data: The timing sheet is already collected for the regional dataset; project charts show case numbers, not names.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients who arrive at night or at weekends, by private car rather than ambulance (no pre-alert), or who need interpreters for the history may not benefit from pre-alert changes. Out-of-hours and walk-in cases are marked on the chart, and interpreter phones are placed in the CT area.
effectiveness: Success is a sustained shift in door-to-needle time with stable haemorrhage, treated mimics at or below 5 percent and no trauma delays.
efficiency: No new staff; a few minutes per case for timing and debrief.
partnerships: Regional ambulance service, emergency department, radiology, pharmacy and two stroke survivors from the regional stroke association.
rebPath: Screened as quality improvement not requiring REB review (QI-SCR-26-203); a publication would follow SQUIRE 2.0.
limitations: Single hospital; about 50 cases; balancing measures too rare to compare statistically.
summary: Low-risk QI under a completed screening, with attention to patients who arrive without pre-alert.
